name: Bradley International Airport
before:
Connecticut's busiest airport and the second largest in New England after Boston, at Windsor Locks. It sits about halfway between Hartford and Springfield, Massachusetts, which makes it useful for clients heading to either.

The terminal arrangement is unusual and easy to get wrong. Terminal A holds almost everything, split across three gate groups: the East Concourse with gates 1 to 12 for Aer Lingus, Delta, Frontier, JetBlue, Southwest and Sun Country, and the West Concourse split between gates 18 to 20 and 21 to 30 for Breeze, American and United. Terminal B is not a terminal in the usual sense at all. It is the International Arrivals Building, used only for flights needing United States customs processing, and it has exactly one gate.

There is one lounge, the Escape Lounge in the East Concourse before gate 1.

Two runways serve the 2,432 acre site. The New England Air Museum is next door, and the airport is shared with the Connecticut Air National Guard.

Frontier and Sun Country rest on Wikipedia alone, and Aer Lingus's Hartford page is a fares template that allows partner connections and even quotes a Chicago flight time, so it does not show a current nonstop. CT Insider also reports that Spirit (which stopped flying here in October 2025) and Avelo have left.

claims.claim: Terminal A holds almost everything, in three gate groups
claims.wasBefore: Terminal A holds almost everything, split across three gate groups
claims.why: Out of date and unconfirmed. CT Insider (27 January 2026) reports that a new concourse with additional gates, an extension of Terminal A, was finished as the last part of a $250 million expansion and was to open within weeks, so the three gate groups are an old picture. The operator's own sites both refused: bradleyairport.com answered the browser with a 403 block page and ctairports.org (Connecticut Airport Authority) with a Cloudflare challenge, so neither was retried. No other source describes the layout now, so the new concourse is not described either (one source only; for Andy).

claims.claim: East Concourse gates 1 to 12 and its airlines, including Aer Lingus, Frontier and Sun Country
claims.wasBefore: the East Concourse with gates 1 to 12 for Aer Lingus, Delta, Frontier, JetBlue, Southwest and Sun Country
claims.why: Gate ranges and concourse allocation rest on Wikipedia alone and predate the 2026 concourse. Delta, JetBlue and Southwest are kept in the airline sentence (BTS, CT Insider). Frontier and Sun Country rest on Wikipedia alone. Aer Lingus is not confirmed: its Hartford page is a fares template that allows partner connections. In review (23 Sep) the airport's own airline page (bradleyairport.com/airlines) was read through the browser tool after a plain fetch met Cloudflare's 'Just a moment' check. It lists these airlines in Terminal A, but it was withdrawn and deleted: the sweep leaves sites behind bot checks alone, so nothing here rests on it. Worth checking by hand; Aer Lingus, Frontier and Sun Country can go back if the airport confirms them.
